annotations.text:
Recreation of Sean's reference photo as the build spec for the v3 coin plate.

This canvas respecs the LOOK only. Behaviour — drag, arm, coin return, keyboard route, reduced motion — stays owned by docs/design/web-redesign/coin-slot-spec.md, which is currently stale against the shipped CSS and needs reconciling either way.

These are not seven candidates to choose one of. A is the floor and the others stack on top of it.

Recommended build: A + D + C + E — gradients for the body, drop-shadow bloom so light comes off the glyphs, turbulence so it stops reading as generated, blend passes so the hot spots warm toward white. Add B if the rib and bosses still look drawn. F and G are the two with real costs; neither is needed at 104×144.

Right-facing profile, as a real quarter carries one. Low-res on purpose — a mark, not a likeness.

Open question for Sean: the reverse. A real quarter has one, and the coin visibly tumbles as it drifts. Leaving it blank is fine; a ghost glyph on the back is the obvious other answer.
